items.name: Potassium
items.role: Helps nerves, muscles and heart rhythm; diets rich in potassium are linked with lower blood pressure.
excess: Dangerously high blood potassium, especially with kidney disease
items.cv_note: Food sources are generally preferred over supplements.
interactions: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, spironolactone: can raise potassium

caution.hypertension: Do not start potassium supplements or salt substitutes without clinician advice.
caution.heart: Rhythm effects at both low and high levels.

items.name: Vitamin K
items.role: Needed for blood clotting factors and bone proteins.
excess: Low toxicity in healthy people; counteracts warfarin

caution.heart: If on warfarin, avoid sudden changes in intake.

items.name: Vitamin D
items.role: Supports calcium absorption and bone health.
excess: High blood calcium, kidney stones, nausea
items.cv_note: Trials have not shown that supplements prevent heart disease in people who are not deficient.

caution.hypertension: Avoid high doses without a measured deficiency.

items.name: Omega-3 fatty acids
items.role: Fish oil fats (EPA, DHA) that lower triglycerides at prescription doses.
excess: Bleeding tendency at high doses; digestive upset
items.cv_note: Eating fish is encouraged; over-the-counter supplements have not consistently reduced events.
interactions: Warfarin and other anticoagulants or antiplatelets (bleeding)

caution.hypertension: Generally low risk at usual doses.
caution.heart: Some trials linked high-dose fish oil to atrial fibrillation: discuss first.

should_you_take: Do you have a measured deficiency (blood test)?
Does your diet plausibly fall short?
Do you take any medicine that interacts?
Does a medical condition make it risky?
